The rise of ADHD isn't driven by technology or better screening. It's driven by incentives for overdiagnosis. 

Schools get more funding, doctors get billable visits, patients get accommodations, and students get cognitive stimulants — all by calling ordinary behavior "hyperactivity." 

The result: overmedication, wasteful spending, and pathological labels, warn Cato’s @AdamOmaryPhD and @dr4liberty.
ow.ly/1pqr50Z1aMi

The Census Bureau is still running webinars to implement OMB's expanded racial data standards for the 2030 Census—in defiance of Trump’s own anti-DEI orders. John F. Early argues the White House must start the administrative process to eliminate SPD 15 before the April 2027 deadline locks it into the census. 

cato.org/blog/president-trum…

This map shows voyages completed under the Jones Act waiver in just over 50 days. 

45 movements, 30+ ports, 35 unique vessels. 

Every voyage is evidence of trade the Jones Act had been blocking for decades. 

Learn more from Cato’s @cpgrabow:
ow.ly/Mjue50Z1RLJ

Subsidies cannot solve the US health sector’s affordability problems. Subsidies are the problem.

Talent and hard work are essential to advancing liberty. The Cato Innovation Project offers a unique opportunity: you design and propose your own full-time role to promote the principles of individual liberty, free markets, and limited government—and Cato provides the funding. 

Applications open now: ow.ly/oYRL50YXKgp

Nicholas Anthony @EconWithNick of the Cato Institute will testify before the House Committee on Financial Services Subcommittee at a hearing titled "Modernizing the BSA for Financial Crime in the 21st Century." 

🔴 Watch live: May 21 at 10 a.m. 
➡️ ow.ly/cpSr50Z1LzH

Can a president punish law firms for who they represent? Cato’s @Thomas_A_Berry argues Trump’s executive orders targeting firms like Perkins Coie are unconstitutional—retaliation for protected advocacy that chills the right to counsel and to challenge government. 

ow.ly/rwxf50Z18mX

It’s fashionable for populists on the left and right to denounce GDP growth as mindless elitism. Yet the US and other countries enjoy longer lives, better health, less poverty, and more happiness because of growth – not despite it. If anything, in fact, GDP underestimates how much things have improved, says Cato’s @scottlincicome.

ow.ly/4pnh50Z1icu

“Immigrants—legal and illegal—work at higher rates, generate more income and taxes, and have reduced the national debt by $14.5 trillion over the last 30 years,” testified Cato’s @David_J_Bier before the House Judiciary Subcommittee.

ow.ly/fNng50Z1hXi

"If the president wants that extraordinary power, the proper course is to ask Congress for it." Section 122 was never designed to impose sweeping tariffs on demand, explain Cato's @clark_packard and @AlfredCObregon.
 
ow.ly/4gNA50Z0qzc
Should the United States Withdraw Troops from Germany? Join us for a discussion featuring: @LianaFix, @jekavanagh, @JustinTLogan, and @katherinet57. nitter.net/i/broadcasts/1AxRnaOra…

Tariff refunds are improving—but many businesses may still struggle to get their money back. Better processing helps, yet delays and red tape can quietly eat into what’s owed. Full refunds should be the baseline, say Cato’s @scottlincicome, @AlfredCObregon, and Chad Smitson. 

ow.ly/E3pH50Z1iIJ

Why do we produce energy? To improve human lives—not to score political points, says @SecretaryWright. 

He argues that every energy policy should be judged by two standards: does it benefit people, and does the math back it up? 

Watch his remarks: piped.video/KGmzgrYNSKk

Video

Does the 14th Amendment guarantee birthright citizenship to persons born in the US to parents without permanent immigration status? Join us for an insightful discussion with a group of scholars who will break down Trump v. Barbara, consider the recent Supreme Court oral argument, and explore the approaches the Court might take as it reaches a decision.
 
Featuring:
🔹 Dan Greenberg, Senior Legal Fellow, Cato Institute
🔹 @IlyaSomin, Professor of Law, George Mason University, and B. Kenneth Simon C

Many Americans think they understand today’s Supreme Court. But Sarah Isgur, host of the Advisory Opinions podcast, editor of @SCOTUSblog, and one of the savviest Court-watchers in the country, is here to tell you that’s wrong.

Join us for a conversation with @whignewtons about what may be the last constitutionally functioning branch of American government.

Register to attend and follow live: ow.ly/upv850Z1ix2

Virginia just banned "assault weapons." Within hours, it was hit with multiple lawsuits. 

One fights it under Virginia's own constitution. The other is designed to ultimately trigger a Supreme Court review. That's the whole point. They want SCOTUS to affirm that modern sporting rifles like the AR-15 are lawful for public ownership under the Second Amendment, says Cato’s @PGEddington. 

cato.org/blog/virginias-assa…

"That's how we create the most flourishing world possible. May the best ideas win." 

Cato Institute President and CEO Peter Goettler joins @spuri on the #RegulatingAI podcast to discuss the benefits of AI, the risks of overregulation, and why the market is the best regulator of all. 
piped.video/jZqUMzH26VY

When policy becomes “government-by-deal,” markets can’t rely on clear, predictable rules. 

Cato’s @DeHavenTad argues that Trump’s new personal financial disclosures highlight the risk of a president making investments while wielding vast discretion over firms—government ownership stakes, export approvals, mergers, and more.  
cato.org/blog/trumps-persona…

Energy Secretary, @SecretaryWright,
says hydrocarbons aren’t running out—we’ve barely scratched the surface. The biggest energy innovations in the coming decades will likely come from oil, gas, and coal.  ow.ly/TEKA50Z0owm
